newsitem.title: USA: Actress Pamela Anderson Lee takes stand in court.
newsitem.headline: Actress Pamela Anderson Lee takes stand in court.

text.p: Actress Pamela Anderson Lee, best known for her role as a swimsuited lifeguard in the TV series "Baywatch," came under fire in court Thursday from a lawyer who accused her of backing out of a movie deal.
Taking the stand for the first time in the non-jury trial, Lee was grilled for about an hour about projects she had agreed to do in the past and some she allegedly backed out of.
"I did not pull out," the blonde actress insisted to attorney Adam Miller, when he suggested she had backed out of the contract to make a movie "Hello, She Lied."

She has been sued for $5 million by The Private Movie Co., which alleged she broke an agreement and pulled out because she had a better offer to make the feature film "Barb Wire," which was subsequently a box-office flop.

The Canadian-born actress, who is married to rock drummer Tommy Lee of the band Motley Crue, claims she changed her mind about making "Hello, She Lied" after seeing the script. She objected because it entailed performing simulated sex, including nude scenes in a shower and on a pool table.

Lee contends she only had a verbal agreement with The Private Movie Co., but the movie-maker says she signed a deal and it had hired other cast members and made arrangements down to details of her security guards and the size of her trailer.
"Hello, She Lied" was later made as "Miami Hustler," with swimsuit model Kathy Ireland in the lead role, and aired on the Showtime cable TV channel.
Lee strode forcefully to the stand in Los Angeles County Court. Asked to state her name, she spelled out "Pamela" in a firm voice.
Miller soon got into a legal argument with defence lawyer Todd Trumper, who objected to the plaintiffs suggesting Lee had a past pattern of breaking contracts.

"I'm going to ask her about entering into agreements ... it goes to her credibility," argued Miller, who said he would show several previous instances of Lee breaking agreements, including one with Virgin Atlantic Airlines "to do something in England she pulled out of."
"I'm allowed to ask this witness about something that goes to her veracity," he said, but Los Angeles Superior Court Judge David Horowitz excluded the line of questioning.
However, the judge allowed Miller to ask Lee about a Playboy video she had initially agreed to shoot.

Lee admitted she backed out, even though she had signed a contract. "I told Hef (Playboy founder Hugh Hefner), a personal friend, I didn't want to do the video at that time and he said 'no problem'", she said.
"They had no problem, they would never sue me," Lee said looking directly at Miller. "I'm very friendly with Playboy."
"They didn't object to Pamela Lee backing out of a video?" he asked incredulously.
"No," she replied. "I get offers all the time."
"I bet you do," Miller shot back, saracastically.
Lee was scheduled to continue her testimony Friday.
